mbpp_0159.reference_description: Write a function to print the season for the given month and day.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to print the season for the given month and day.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SeasonFinder - Determine season from month and day
Goal: Return a season (winter, spring, summer, autumn) for a given month and number of days by mapping months to seasons and then adjusting boundaries using specific day thresholds (e.g., March >19 → spring, June >20 → summer, etc.).

mbpp_0771.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given expression is balanced or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given expression is balanced or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: ExpressionChecker: Balanced Bracket Validator — Main goal: Use a stack to determine if a string has properly balanced and nested (), {}, and [] brackets. It pushes opening brackets, pops and checks matching on closing brackets, and returns true only if all openings are matched and the stack is empty at the end. It also rejects odd-length expressions early and ignores non-bracket characters during processing.

mbpp_0323.reference_description: Write a function to re-arrange the given array in alternating positive and negative items.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to re-arrange the given array in alternating positive and negative items.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: This code rearranges an integer array in place to achieve alternating signs: negative values at even indices and non-negative values at odd indices. It tracks the next out-of-place index, finds a later element with the opposite sign, right-rotates the subarray to bring that element into the out-of-place position, and updates the next target index until the entire array conforms to the pattern.

mbpp_0189.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first missing positive number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first missing positive number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: First Missing Positive - In-Place Marking
Goal: Return the smallest positive integer not present in the array in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
Approach: Normalize the array to contain only values 1..n (replacing others with 1), then for each value arr[i], mark the presence of (arr[i] - 1) by adding n to the corresponding index. Finally, the first index with a value still ≤ n indicates the missing number (index + 1); if all are > n after marking, return n + 1.

mbpp_0245.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum sum of bi-tonic sub-sequence for the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum sum of bi-tonic sub-sequence for the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: Find the maximum-sum bitonic subsequence in an array. The code computes, for each index i, the best sum of an increasing subsequence ending at i (MSIBS), and the best sum of a decreasing subsequence starting at i (MSDBS), then takes the maximum of MSIBS[i] + MSDBS[i] − arr[i] to get the maximum sum of a bitonic subsequence with peak at i. Time complexity is O(n^2) and auxiliary space is O(n).

mbpp_0522.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest bitonic subsequence for the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest bitonic subsequence for the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Bitonic Subsequence Length Calculator

Main goal: Compute the length of the longest bitonic subsequence (an increasing sequence followed by a decreasing sequence) in the given array. It builds two DP arrays: lis[i] for the longest increasing subsequence ending at i, and lds[i] for the longest decreasing subsequence starting at i, then combines them as lis[i] + lds[i] - 1 and returns the maximum. The subsequences are strictly increasing/decreasing due to the use of the '>' comparison. Complexity is O(n^2) time and O(n) extra space.

mbpp_0776.reference_description: Write a function to count those characters which have vowels as their neighbors in the given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count those characters which have vowels as their neighbors in the given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Count consonants adjacent to vowels
Main goal: Given a string, count how many lowercase non-vowel characters (i.e., consonants) are immediately adjacent to at least one vowel (a, e, i, o, u). It checks interior positions and also handles the first and last characters. Returns the count as an integer.

mbpp_0039.reference_description: Write a function to check if the letters of a given string can be rearranged so that two characters that are adjacent to each other are different.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the letters of a given string can be rearranged so that two characters that are adjacent to each other are different.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: Reorganize the input string so that no two adjacent characters are the same. It counts character frequencies, uses a max-heap to repeatedly take the two most frequent distinct characters, appends them, and decrements their counts. If any character occurs more than (length + 1) / 2 times, it returns an empty string. The Node class stores a character and its remaining count.

mbpp_0069.reference_description: Write a function to check whether array contains the given sublist or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether array contains the given sublist or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SublistChecker
Main goal: Determine if a list s is a contiguous sublist of another list l.

Brief description: The static generic method isSublist checks if s is empty or equal to l (true), or if s is longer than l (false). Otherwise, it slides a window over l and compares each possible subsegment with s; it returns true if a full match is found, and false if no match exists.

mbpp_0223.reference_description: Write a function to check for majority element in the given sorted array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check for majority element in the given sorted array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Majority Element Check in a Sorted Array
Main goal: Determine whether x is a majority element (appears more than n/2 times) in the sorted array arr of length n by finding the first occurrence of x with a binary search and then verifying that the element at index i + n/2 is also x; returns true if so, otherwise false.

mbpp_0123.reference_description: Write a function to sum all amicable numbers from 1 to a specified number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sum all amicable numbers from 1 to a specified number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
- Title: Amicable Numbers Sum Calculator
- Main goal: Given a limit, find amicable number pairs where at least one member is within the limit and return the sum of all numbers that appear in such pairs.
- How it works: For each number from 2 to limit, compute the sum of its proper divisors, then compute the sum of proper divisors of that result. If they form a mutual pair (a's sum is b, and b's sum is a, with a ≠ b), add both numbers to a set (to avoid duplicates). After the loop, sum all numbers in the set and return the total.
- Supporting function: sumOfDivisors(n) returns the sum of all positive divisors of n less than n.
- Notes: The final sum may include amicable partners greater than the limit (if their partner is within the limit). Time complexity is roughly O(limit^2) due to divisor summation up to n for each n.

mbpp_0515.reference_description: Write a function to check if there is a subset with sum divisible by m.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if there is a subset with sum divisible by m.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Subset sum divisibility by m
Main goal: Determine whether there exists a non-empty subset of the given array whose sum is a multiple of m. It uses a dynamic programming approach over remainders modulo m: DP[r] indicates that a subset with sum ≡ r (mod m) has been found. It iterates through the elements, updating reachable remainders, and returns true as soon as remainder 0 becomes reachable. It also short-circuits with n > m (pigeonhole principle) to always return true; otherwise, it returns false if no such subset exists after processing all elements.

mbpp_0423.reference_description: Write a function to solve gold mine problem.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to solve gold mine problem.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum Gold in a Grid (Dynamic Programming)

Main goal: Compute the maximum amount of gold that can be collected by starting from any row in the first column and moving to the last column, at each step moving to the cell to the right, right-up, or right-down. The code uses dynamic programming to fill a DP table from right to left and returns the maximum value found in the first column.

mbpp_0747.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given three string sequence.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given three string sequence.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: LCS of Three Strings (LCS3) via 3D Dynamic Programming
Main goal: Given three strings X, Y, Z, compute the length of their longest common subsequence using a 3D DP table L[m+1][n+1][o+1]. It initializes zeros when any string is empty, increments when the current characters of all three match, and otherwise takes the maximum LCS length by excluding one character from any of the strings. Returns L[m][n][o], the length of the longest common subsequence.

mbpp_0408.reference_description: Write a function to find k number of pairs which consist of one element from the first array and one element from the second array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find k number of pairs which consist of one element from the first array and one element from the second array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: K smallest pairs by sum using a min-heap
Main goal: Given two sorted arrays, return up to k pairs (nums1[i], nums2[j]) with the smallest sums nums1[i] + nums2[j]. The code maintains a min-heap of candidates [sum, i, j], begins with (0,0), iteratively extracts the smallest pair, adds it to the result, and pushes the next candidates (i, j+1) and (i+1, j) when appropriate, until k results are produced or inputs are exhausted. Assumes nums1 and nums2 are sorted in non-decreasing order.

mbpp_0838.reference_description: Write a java function to find minimum number swaps required to make two binary strings equal.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find minimum number swaps required to make two binary strings equal.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code computes the minimum number of swaps needed to make two binary strings s1 and s2 equal by swapping characters within the strings. It counts mismatches of two types: c0 = positions where s1 has 0 and s2 has 1, and c1 = positions where s1 has 1 and s2 has 0. If (c0 + c1) is odd, it returns -1 (impossible). Otherwise, it uses base = c0/2 + c1/2; if both c0 and c1 are even, it returns base; if both are odd, it returns base + 2 (two extra swaps); this aligns with the minimum swaps needed in this scenario.

mbpp_0940.reference_description: Write a function to sort the given array by using heap sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort the given array by using heap sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: In-place heap sort implementation. The code builds a max-heap from the input array and then sorts it in ascending order by repeatedly swapping the maximum element (index 0) with the last unsorted element and sifting down the new root to restore the heap. It consists of three methods: heapSort (drives the process), heapify (builds the initial max-heap by sifting down from the middle toward the root), and shiftDown (performs the sift-down to maintain the max-heap property). Time complexity is O(n log n) and it uses O(1) extra space since it sorts in place. The result is a sorted array in ascending order.

mbpp_0387.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the hexadecimal number is even or odd.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the hexadecimal number is even or odd.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Hexadecimal parity checker
Main goal: Determine whether a given hexadecimal number (as a string N) is even or odd by inspecting its least-significant hex digit; returns "Even" if the last digit is 0,2,4,6,8,A,C, or E; otherwise returns "Odd".

mbpp_0628.reference_description: Write a function to replace all spaces in the given string with character * array item * array item * array item * array item '%20'.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to replace all spaces in the given string with character * array item * array item * array item * array item '%20'.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: URL-Style Space Encoding (replace spaces with %20)

Main goal: Given a string, trim it, count spaces, and produce a new string where each space is replaced by "%20" by expanding the character array from the end. If the resulting length exceeds a fixed MAX of 1000, return "-1". The method returns the transformed string with spaces encoded as %20.

mbpp_0315.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first maximum length of even word.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first maximum length of even word.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Parses the input string by spaces to find the longest word with an even number of characters; it returns that word, or "-1" if no even-length word exists. It scans in one pass, tracking the current word length and its start index, and updates the result when a space (or end) completes an even-length word.

mbpp_0516.reference_description: Write a function to sort array of elements using radix sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort array of elements using radix sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Java LSD Radix Sort Implementation
Main goal: Sort an array of non-negative integers using a base-10 least-significant-digit radix sort. The code finds the maximum value to estimate digit passes, then iteratively distributes numbers into ten buckets by the current digit (i / place) % 10, concatenates the buckets back into the array, and advances to the next digit by multiplying place by 10. It returns the sorted array.
Note: There is a potential off-by-one bug in the loop condition (placement < maxDigit) which can skip processing the most significant digit for some inputs, since maxDigit is the maximum value, not the digit count.

mbpp_0834.reference_description: Write a function to generate a square matrix filled with elements from 1 to n raised to the power of 2 in spiral order.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to generate a square matrix filled with elements from 1 to n raised to the power of 2 in spiral order.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Spiral Matrix Generator
Main goal: Generate an n x n matrix filled with numbers 1 to n^2 in clockwise spiral order, starting from the top-left corner.
Approach: Uses four moving boundaries (rowStart, rowEnd, colStart, colEnd) and fills the top row left-to-right, the right column top-to-bottom, the bottom row right-to-left, and the left column bottom-to-top in a loop until all cells are filled; handles non-positive n by returning an empty matrix.

mbpp_0152.reference_description: Write a function to sort the given array by using merge sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort the given array by using merge sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Implements the merge sort algorithm for integer arrays. The merge(a,b) method merges two sorted arrays into a single sorted array in ascending order. The mergeSort(x) method recursively splits the array into halves, sorts each half, and then merges them, returning a new sorted array. Handles null or length-1 inputs by returning the input as is.

mbpp_0901.reference_description: Write a function to find the smallest multiple of the first n numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the smallest multiple of the first n numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SmallestMultiple
Main goal: For a given n, compute the smallest multiple of n that is divisible by every integer greater than n/2 up to n (i.e., the least common multiple of the range floor(n/2)+1 .. n). The code collects those numbers and then iteratively checks multiples of n until one is divisible by all collected factors, returning that value.

mbpp_0501.reference_description: Write a java function to find common divisor between two numbers in a given pair.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find common divisor between two numbers in a given pair.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: CommonDivisors
Main goal: Compute the greatest common divisor of two integers using a naive trial method, then count how many positive divisors that gcd has (i.e., the number of common divisors of the two numbers).
Functions:
- ngcd(int x, int y): Brute-force gcd by testing all integers from 1 to min(x, y) and updating the gcd when both x and y are divisible by that integer.
- numCommDiv(int x, int y): Uses ngcd to obtain n = gcd(x, y), then counts the number of positive divisors of n by iterating up to sqrt(n), adding 2 for each divisor pair, and subtracting 1 if n is a perfect square.

mbpp_0938.reference_description: Write a function to find three closest elements from three sorted arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find three closest elements from three sorted arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: pick one element from each array A, B, and C (sizes p, q, r) so that the range among the three selected values (max - min) is minimized. It uses three pointers i, j, k starting at 0 and always advances the pointer pointing to the current minimum value, updating the best triplet when a tighter range is found, and stops early if a perfect match (diff = 0) is found. Returns the triple (A[resI], B[resJ], C[resK]). Time complexity: O(p + q + r); space complexity: O(1).

mbpp_0898.reference_description: Write a function to extract specified number of elements from a given array, which follow each other continuously.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract specified number of elements from a given array, which follow each other continuously.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Extractor.extractElements
Main goal: From a list of integers, return values that occur in runs of exactly n consecutive identical numbers; handles null/empty lists or n <= 0 by returning an empty list; duplicates may appear if multiple runs of length n exist.

mbpp_0665.reference_description: Write a java function to shift first element to the end of given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to shift first element to the end of given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Move all occurrences of the first element to the end
Main goal: Given a list of integers, return a new list where every occurrence of the first element is removed from its original position and appended at the end in the same count. If the input is null or empty, return an empty list. The input list is not mutated.

mbpp_0822.reference_description: Write a function to return true if the password is valid.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to return true if the password is valid.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: PasswordValidator
Main goal: Validate a password based on length and character rules
Summary: The passValidity method checks that the input string p is 6–12 characters long, contains at least one lowercase letter, one digit, one uppercase letter, and at least one of the symbols $, #, or @, and contains no whitespace. Returns true if all conditions are met; otherwise returns false.

mbpp_0149.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest subsequence such that the difference between adjacents is one for the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest subsequence such that the difference between adjacents is one for the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Subsequence with Adjacent Difference One
Main goal: Determine the length of the longest subsequence (not necessarily contiguous) in which consecutive elements differ by exactly 1. Uses dynamic programming: dp[i] stores the best length of a subsequence ending at index i; initialize to 1, and for each i, check all j < i, updating dp[i] if arr[i] and arr[j] differ by 1. The final result is the maximum value in dp. Time complexity: O(n^2); Space complexity: O(n).

mbpp_0060.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum length of the subsequence with difference between adjacent elements for the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum length of the subsequence with difference between adjacent elements for the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxLenSub — Longest subsequence with adjacent elements differing by at most 1
Main goal: Given an array, determine the length of the longest non-contiguous subsequence where the absolute difference between consecutive elements is at most 1. It uses dynamic programming with mls[i] representing the longest valid subsequence ending at i; initialized to 1, it checks all earlier indices j and extends mls[i] when abs(arr[i] - arr[j]) <= 1, finally returning the maximum value in mls.

mbpp_0548.reference_description: Write a function to find the length of the longest increasing subsequence of the given sequence.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the length of the longest increasing subsequence of the given sequence.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Increasing Subsequence Length
Main goal: Compute and return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence in the input array using dynamic programming (O(n^2)), by tracking the LIS ending at each position and taking the maximum.

mbpp_0468.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum product formed by multiplying numbers of an increasing subsequence of that array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum product formed by multiplying numbers of an increasing subsequence of that array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Max Product Increasing Subsequence
Main goal: Compute the maximum product obtainable from a strictly increasing subsequence of the input array. It uses dynamic programming: mpis[i] stores the maximum product of an increasing subsequence ending at i, initialized to arr[i], and updated by extending from earlier indices j where arr[i] > arr[j]. The result is the maximum value in mpis. Time complexity is O(n^2) and space complexity is O(n).

mbpp_0550.reference_description: Write a java function to find the maximum element in a sorted and rotated array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the maximum element in a sorted and rotated array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Binary search for the peak in a bitonic array
Main goal: Locate and return the maximum (peak) element of a bitonic array (one that monotonically increases then decreases) by recursively narrowing the index range using binary-search logic.

mbpp_0524.reference_description: Write a function to find the sum of maximum increasing subsequence of the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the sum of maximum increasing subsequence of the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: Find the maximum sum of any strictly increasing subsequence in the input array (maximum sum increasing subsequence, MSIS) using dynamic programming. It maintains msis[i] as the best sum of an increasing subsequence ending at i (initialized to arr[i]), updates it by checking all j < i with arr[i] > arr[j], and returns the largest msis value (bounded by 0 as a baseline if all sums are negative).

mbpp_0523.reference_description: Write a function to check whether a given string has a capital letter, a lower case letter, a number and specified length using lambda function.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether a given string has a capital letter, a lower case letter, a number and specified length using lambda function.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Multi-criteria String Validator (uppercase, lowercase, digit, length)

Main goal: Validate an input string against four requirements by applying a set of functional checks. It returns a list of error messages for any unmet criteria, or ["Valid string."] if all checks pass. Note: there is a mismatch between the length check (>=7) and the message ("at least 8"), indicating a bug.

mbpp_0926.reference_description: Write a function to find n-th rencontres number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find n-th rencontres number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Calculating rencontres numbers (permutations with a given number of fixed points)
Main goal: Implement recursive computation of binomial coefficients and the number of permutations of n with exactly m fixed points (rencontres numbers). Specifically, rencontresNumber(n,m) returns C(n,m) * D(n−m), where D(k) (the number of derangements) is defined by D(0)=1, D(1)=0, and D(k)=(k−1)[D(k−1)+D(k−2)]. The binomialCoeff(n,k) is computed recursively using Pascal's rule.

mbpp_0881.reference_description: Write a function to find the sum of first even and odd number of a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the sum of first even and odd number of a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Sum of first even and first odd elements in a list
Main goal: Given a list of integers, locate the first even number and the first odd number, then return their sum. The method scans the list, stores the first occurrences in firstEven and firstOdd, and stops when both are found. If either is missing, -1 is used as a placeholder, so the result could be even-1, odd-1, or -2 if neither is found.

mbpp_0068.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given array is monotonic or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the given array is monotonic or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Checks whether the input int array is monotonic (entirely non-decreasing or non-increasing). It returns true for null or length < 2. It scans the array once, updating two flags (nonDecreasing and nonIncreasing) and returns false only if both flags become false; otherwise returns true.

mbpp_0755.reference_description: Write a function to find the second smallest number in array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the second smallest number in array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SecondSmallestFinder - returns second smallest distinct integer from a list.
Main goal: Given a list of integers, compute the second smallest unique value and return it; handle nulls and cases with fewer than two distinct values by returning null. It builds a list of unique values in input order, sorts them, and returns the second element if present; otherwise null.

mbpp_0907.reference_description: Write a function to print the first n lucky numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to print the first n lucky numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Lucky Numbers Sieve (Java)

Main goal: Generate the first n lucky numbers using a sieve-like process and print them.

What it does (brief): Builds a list starting with -1 followed by odd numbers. Repeatedly uses the i-th surviving value as a step to remove every step-th element from the list, updating the list each time. After finishing, returns the first n numbers (excluding the initial -1). The main method reads n from command-line, computes these numbers, and prints them.

mbpp_0866.reference_description: Write a function to check whether the given month name contains 31 days or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether the given month name contains 31 days or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: 31-Day Month Checker
Main goal: Implement a helper MonthUtil.checkMonthNumb(String) that returns true if the given month name is one of the seven months with 31 days (January, March, May, July, August, October, December); otherwise returns false. It uses a switch statement with multiple cases mapping to true, and a default to false. Note: exact string matching; no null or case-insensitive handling.

mbpp_0455.reference_description: Write a function to check whether the given month number contains 31 days or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether the given month number contains 31 days or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MonthUtils.checkMonthNumber - 31-day-month detector
Main goal: Determine whether a given numeric month corresponds to a 31-day month (returns true) or not (returns false).
What it does: checkMonthNumber(int monthnum2) returns true if monthnum2 is 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, or 12; otherwise it returns false.

mbpp_0850.reference_description: Write a function to check if a triangle of positive area is possible with the given angles.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if a triangle of positive area is possible with the given angles.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Triangle angle validator
Main goal: Determine if three integers can be the angles of a triangle by verifying they are non-zero and sum to 180 (the inner inequality check is redundant); it will return true for valid angle triples, but it can incorrectly accept some invalid inputs like negatives that sum to 180.

mbpp_0463.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum product subarray of the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum product subarray of the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum Product Subarray (Variant)
Main goal: Given an array of integers, compute the maximum product of any contiguous subarray by dynamically tracking the maximum and minimum product ending at each position, while handling positives, negatives, and zeros. The method uses maxEndingHere and minEndingHere to propagate products, resets on zero, and keeps maxSoFar as the best product found. It returns 0 if no positive product exists (e.g., all negatives with no zeros), otherwise it returns the maximum product found.

mbpp_0074.reference_description: Write a function to check whether it follows the sequence given in the patterns array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether it follows the sequence given in the patterns array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Checks whether the colors array follows the same pattern as the patterns array by enforcing a bijective mapping: each unique pattern maps to a single color and no two patterns share the same color. Returns true if the mapping is consistent across all positions; otherwise false.

mbpp_0453.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of even factors of a number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of even factors of a number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Sum of Even Divisors Calculator

Main goal: Given an input n, compute the sum of all even divisors of n. If n is odd, return 0. The code factorizes n into prime powers and multiplies the sums of each prime power series, with a special handling for the prime 2 that excludes the 2^0 term, effectively yielding the sum of all even divisors of n.

mbpp_0031.reference_description: Write a function to find the top k integers that occur most frequently from given arrays of sorted and distinct integers using heap queue algorithm.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the top k integers that occur most frequently from given arrays of sorted and distinct integers using heap queue algorithm.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: return the k most frequent integers found across the nested list nums. It counts how many times each integer appears, then maintains a min-heap of size k to keep the top k frequencies. Finally, it extracts and returns the corresponding integers (in ascending frequency order; ties may be unordered).

mbpp_0854.reference_description: Write a function which accepts an arbitrary array and converts it to a heap using heap queue algorithm.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function which accepts an arbitrary array and converts it to a heap using heap queue algorithm.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: In-place heapify to a min-heap
Main goal: Build a min-heap from an arbitrary List<T> by applying a bottom-up sift-down (heapify) algorithm; the method rawHeap converts the list in place and returns it, for elements comparable via T extends Comparable.

mbpp_0469.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum profit earned from a maximum of k stock transactions

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum profit earned from a maximum of k stock transactions
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum Profit with At Most k Stock Transactions (Dynamic Programming)
Main goal: Compute the maximum profit obtainable from at most k buy-sell transactions on a given price array, using a 2D DP table finalProfit[i][j] where i is the number of transactions and j is the day index. The DP considers either skipping the current day or selling on the current day after buying on an earlier day, building on solutions with fewer transactions.

mbpp_0129.reference_description: Write a function to calculate magic square.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate magic square.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MagicSquareTest
Main goal: Determine if a given square matrix is a magic square by verifying that all row sums, all column sums, and both diagonal sums are equal; returns true if they all match.

What it does:
- Computes sums of all rows and stores them
- Computes sums of all columns and stores them
- Computes the main diagonal sum and stores it
- Attempts to compute the secondary diagonal sum, but uses the wrong indices (myMatrix[i][i] instead of myMatrix[i][iSize-1-i]), so the anti-diagonal check is incorrect
- Converts all collected sums to a Set and checks that there is at most one unique sum (size <= 1)

Notes: Assumes a square matrix; the anti-diagonal calculation contains a bug that can affect correctness.

mbpp_0113.reference_description: Write a function to check if a string represents an integer or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if a string represents an integer or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: IntegerChecker.checkInteger
Main goal: Check if a given string represents a valid decimal integer (optional '+' or '-' sign) after trimming; returns true for valid integers, false for invalid characters, and null if the input is empty after trimming or consists only of a sign.

mbpp_0382.reference_description: Write a function to find the number of rotations in a circularly sorted array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the number of rotations in a circularly sorted array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: RotationCounter — Find the rotation count in a rotated sorted array
Main goal: Use a binary-search approach to locate the pivot (the smallest element) in a rotated sorted array and return its index, which equals the number of times the array was rotated (0 if already sorted). It handles edge cases and considers circular neighbors (next/prev).

mbpp_0639.reference_description: Write a function to sum the length of the names of a given array of names after removing the names that start with a lowercase letter.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sum the length of the names of a given array of names after removing the names that start with a lowercase letter.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Sum lengths of properly capitalized names
Main goal: Compute the total length of strings in the input list that have length > 1, start with an uppercase letter, and have all remaining characters lowercase; return the sum of those lengths.

mbpp_0306.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum sum of increasing subsequence from prefix till ith index and also including a given kth element which is after i, i.e., k > i .

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum sum of increasing subsequence from prefix till ith index and also including a given kth element which is after i, i.e., k > i .
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxSumIncreasingSubseq - 2D DP approach for Maximum Sum Increasing Subsequence

Main goal: Attempt to compute the maximum sum of an increasing subsequence from the input array a using a two-dimensional DP table (dp). It initializes base values for the first element and then fills dp with a transition when a[j] > a[i] and j > i, otherwise propagating previous values, finally returning dp[index][k]. Note that the DP formulation and indices appear nonstandard and may not correctly solve the conventional maximum-sum increasing subsequence problem.

mbpp_0247.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest palindromic subsequence in the given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest palindromic subsequence in the given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Dynamic Programming approach for Longest Palindromic Subsequence Length

Main goal: Given a string, compute the length of its longest palindromic subsequence by filling a 2D DP table L where L[i][j] stores the LPS length for substring i..j. It initializes L[i][i] = 1, then processes substrings of increasing length: if the end characters match, it uses L[i+1][j-1] (+2 or 2 for length 2); otherwise it takes the maximum of L[i][j-1] and L[i+1][j]. The result is L[0][n-1].

mbpp_0466.reference_description: Write a function to find the peak element in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the peak element in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Binary-search-based peak finder: recursively locates an index i where arr[i] is greater than or equal to its neighbors (a peak). findPeak is a wrapper that initiates the search over the full array, returning the peak index in O(log n) time.

mbpp_0107.reference_description: Write a java function to count hexadecimal numbers for a given range.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count hexadecimal numbers for a given range.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Hexadecimal-digit counter over a range
Main goal: Return the total number of hexadecimal digits in all numbers from L to R that are letters A–F (digits with value 10–15) in their hex representation.
How it works: For each i in [L, R], if 10–15 it contributes 1; if greater than 15 it iterates over its base-16 digits (via modulo 16 and division by 16) and increments the count for each digit >= 10.

mbpp_0689.reference_description: ## write a function to find the minimum number of jumps to reach the end of the array for the given array of integers where each element represents the max number of steps that can be made forward from that element. > indented block > indented block

Description_Simple.reference_text: ## write a function to find the minimum number of jumps to reach the end of the array for the given array of integers where each element represents the max number of steps that can be made forward from that element. > indented block > indented block
Description_Simple.comparison_text: This is a dynamic programming solution that tries to compute the minimum number of jumps needed to reach the last index of an array, where each arr[i] is the maximum jump length from position i. It uses a jumps[] array, with jumps[0] = 0, and for each position i it looks for a predecessor j that can reach i (i <= j + arr[j]) and updates jumps[i] accordingly. It returns jumps[n-1] (or Integer.MAX_VALUE if unreachable). Note: there is a bug due to breaking the inner loop after the first valid predecessor, which can yield incorrect results, and the initial edge-case handling may mishandle trivial cases like n == 1.

mbpp_0239.reference_description: Write a function to find the number of possible sequences of length n such that each of the next element is greater than or equal to twice of the previous element but less than or equal to m.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the number of possible sequences of length n such that each of the next element is greater than or equal to twice of the previous element but less than or equal to m.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SequenceCounter (dynamic programming)

Main goal: Compute the number of sequences of length n with elements bounded by m using a bottom-up DP. The 2D table T[i][j] is filled with the recurrence T[i][j] = T[i-1][j] + T[i/2][j-1], with base cases T[i][1] = i and T[i][j] = 0 when i == 0, j == 0, or i < j; the result returned is T[m][n].

mbpp_0885.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the two given strings are isomorphic to each other or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the two given strings are isomorphic to each other or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Isomorphic Strings by Position Pattern
Main goal: Determine if two strings are isomorphic by collecting, for each distinct character, the list of its indices in the string, sorting these index-lists, and comparing the multisets of index-lists between the two strings. If the multisets match, the strings have a one-to-one character mapping; otherwise they do not.

mbpp_0121.reference_description: Write a function to find the triplet with sum of the given array

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the triplet with sum of the given array
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Recursive Triplet Sum Checker
Main goal: Determine if there exists a subset of exactly three elements from array A (length n) whose sum equals the given target sum. The function uses recursion to either include or exclude each element, tracking the remaining sum and the number of elements chosen, returning true if a 3-element subset sums to the target, otherwise false.

mbpp_0826.reference_description: Write a java function to find the type of triangle from the given sides.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the type of triangle from the given sides.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Determines if a triangle with sides a, b, c is right-, obtuse-, or acute-angled by comparing squared sides; however, it contains a bug in the right-angle check (uses sqa == sqa + sqb, etc.) and lacks triangle validity checks and proper floating-point handling.

mbpp_0108.reference_description: Write a function to merge multiple sorted inputs into a single sorted iterator using heap queue algorithm.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to merge multiple sorted inputs into a single sorted iterator using heap queue algorithm.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Merge three sorted lists into one using a min-heap

Main goal: Combine num1, num2, and num3 into a single sorted list in ascending order. The code first sorts each input list, then uses a PriorityQueue as a min-heap where each Node stores the current value and its source iterator. It seeds the heap with the first element from each list, repeatedly extracts the smallest value, appends it to the result, and pushes the next element from the corresponding iterator until all lists are exhausted.

mbpp_0231.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum sum in the given right triangle of numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum sum in the given right triangle of numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: In-place Dynamic Programming for Triangle Maximum Path Sum
Main goal: Given a triangular 2D array, compute the maximum sum from the triangle's top to bottom by updating each cell to store the best sum to reach that position, and return the maximum value on the bottom row.

mbpp_0485.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest palindromic number in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest palindromic number in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
PalindromeUtils — Largest Palindrome in an Array

Main goal: Find the largest palindrome number in a given integer array (or -1 if none). It uses isPalindrome to test numbers by comparing leading and trailing digits, and largestPalindrome sorts the array and returns the largest element that is a palindrome.

mbpp_0181.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest common prefix in the given set of strings.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest common prefix in the given set of strings.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: compute the longest common prefix (LCP) among a given array of strings. The helper commonPrefixUtil compares two strings character by character to build their shared prefix, and commonPrefix iteratively folds this across the first n elements of the array, returning an empty string if n is 0.

mbpp_0570.reference_description: Write a function to remove words from a given array of strings containing a character or string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to remove words from a given array of strings containing a character or string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: RemoveWordsUtil – Filter words by forbidden substrings

Main goal: Given a list of lines (list1) and a list of phrases (charlist), for each line, split into words, remove any word that contains any phrase from charlist, then rejoin the remaining words into a new line. Return the list of these processed lines.

mbpp_0397.reference_description: Write a function to find the median of three specific numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the median of three specific numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MedianFinder - Find the median of three integers
Main goal: Return the middle value among three input integers a, b, and c using nested if-else comparisons (without sorting).

mbpp_0685.reference_description: Write a java function to find sum of prime numbers between 1 to n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find sum of prime numbers between 1 to n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Sum of primes up to n using a sieve
Main goal: Return the sum of all prime numbers less than or equal to n. It builds a boolean primality array, uses the Sieve of Eratosthenes to mark non-prime numbers, then sums all indices marked prime and returns the total.

mbpp_0863.reference_description: Write a function to find the length of the longest sub-sequence such that elements in the subsequences are consecutive integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the length of the longest sub-sequence such that elements in the subsequences are consecutive integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Consecutive Subsequence Length Finder
Main goal: Given an array, compute the length of the longest run of consecutive integers present in the array. It sorts the array, removes duplicates to form unique values, then scans to count consecutive sequences (incrementing when current equals previous plus one, otherwise resetting) and returns the maximum length found. Assumes non-empty input; may throw if n == 0. Complexity: O(n log n) due to sorting.

mbpp_0526.reference_description: Write a java function to capitalize first and last letters of each word of a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to capitalize first and last letters of each word of a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Capitalize first and last letters of each word
Main goal: Transform a string so that every word has its first and last letters capitalized while the middle letters remain lowercase; single-letter words are capitalized; spaces are normalized to single spaces.

mbpp_0943.reference_description: Write a function to combine two given sorted arrays using heapq module.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to combine two given sorted arrays using heapq module.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Goal: Combine two sorted lists into one sorted list by merging them with a two-pointer approach.
Function: combineLists takes two List<Integer> inputs, iterates through both with indices i and j, appending the smaller current element (using <= to favor elements from the first list on ties), and then appends any remaining elements from either list. Returns the merged, sorted list.
Complexity: Time O(n + m); Space O(n + m) for the new list.

mbpp_0971.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum number of segments of lengths a, b and c that can be formed from n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum number of segments of lengths a, b and c that can be formed from n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Dynamic Programming for Maximum Rope Segments
Main goal: Given a length n and three segment lengths a, b, and c, compute the maximum number of segments that can sum exactly to n (return -1 if impossible). The code uses a 1D DP array where dp[i] stores the maximum number of pieces to achieve length i (initialized to -1, with dp[0] = 0). It iterates i from 0 to n-1 and, when reachable, updates dp[i+a], dp[i+b], and dp[i+c] by dp[i] + 1. The answer is dp[n].

mbpp_0632.reference_description: Write a java function to move all zeroes to the end of the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to move all zeroes to the end of the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Move zeros to the end - Returns a new list where all non-zero elements from the input retain their order, followed by all zeros; input is not modified in place.

mbpp_0745.reference_description: Write a function to find numbers within a given range where every number is divisible by every digit it contains.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find numbers within a given range where every number is divisible by every digit it contains.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Finds all integers n in the inclusive range [startnum, endnum] that are divisible by every nonzero decimal digit they contain; numbers with a 0 digit are discarded. Returns these numbers as a list.

mbpp_0054.reference_description: Write a function to sort the given array by using counting sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort the given array by using counting sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: CountingSort: A static method that sorts an int array in ascending order using the counting sort algorithm. It finds the maximum value to size a frequency bucket, tallies occurrences of each value, then rebuilds the original array in sorted order and returns it.

mbpp_0256.reference_description: Write a java function to count the number of prime numbers less than a given non-negative number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the number of prime numbers less than a given non-negative number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: PrimeCounter — Main goal: count how many prime numbers are strictly less than n by testing each candidate with a naive trial-division primality check and returning the total count.

mbpp_0620.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest subset where each pair is divisible.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest subset where each pair is divisible.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Divisible Subsequence (order-preserving)

Main goal: Return the length of the longest subsequence (in the given order) where each adjacent pair satisfies divisibility (one number divides the other). It uses bottom-up DP: for each i, dp[i] = 1 + max(dp[j]) over j > i with a[i] and a[j] divisible; the final result is the maximum dp[i].

mbpp_0597.reference_description: Write a function to find kth element from the given two sorted arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find kth element from the given two sorted arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: KthElementFinder
Goal: Merge two sorted arrays into a single sorted array and return the k-th smallest element (as merged[k-1]); uses a two-pointer merge to build the combined array.

mbpp_0476.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of the largest and smallest value in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of the largest and smallest value in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Sum of min and max in an integer array
Main goal: Given an int array, validate it is non-null and non-empty, determine the smallest and largest elements, and return their sum (min + max). Throws IllegalArgumentException if input is null or empty.

mbpp_0415.reference_description: Write a java function to find a pair with highest product from a given array of integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find a pair with highest product from a given array of integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxProduct — Find the two elements with the maximum product
Main goal: Given an int array, return the pair of distinct elements whose product is the largest (brute-force O(n^2) approach).
What it does: Validates input (throws if null or fewer than two elements), initializes a candidate pair with the first two elements, iterates over all pairs to find the maximum product, updates the pair when a larger product is found, and returns the pair as int[]{x, y}.

mbpp_0922.reference_description: Write a function to find a pair with the highest product from a given array of integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find a pair with the highest product from a given array of integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxProductFinder - Brute-force max product pair finder
Main goal: Given an int array, return the pair of elements whose product is maximal. It uses a nested loop to examine all unique pairs, tracks the best pair (x, y), and compares products using long to avoid overflow. Returns null if input is invalid (null or fewer than 2 elements); otherwise returns an array [x, y].

mbpp_0588.reference_description: Write a java function to find the difference between largest and smallest value in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the difference between largest and smallest value in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: BigDiff: Calculates the range (max - min) of a non-empty int array by scanning for min and max; throws IllegalArgumentException if the input is null or empty.

mbpp_0751.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given array represents min heap or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given array represents min heap or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: MinHeapChecker – Main goal: determine recursively whether an array represents a min-heap. The method checkMinHeap(arr, i) verifies that the node at index i is <= its left child (if present) and <= its right child (if present), recursing on children; it handles leaves and missing children as base cases and returns true if the entire subtree rooted at i satisfies the min-heap property.

mbpp_0342.reference_description: Write a function to find the smallest range that includes at-least one element from each of the given arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the smallest range that includes at-least one element from each of the given arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Smallest Range Across k Sorted Lists
Main goal: Given several sorted lists, determine the smallest interval [low, high] that contains at least one element from each list. This is achieved by using a min-heap (priority queue) to repeatedly take the smallest current value from the lists, while tracking the current maximum value seen (high). After each extraction, update the best range if the current [low, high] is smaller, push the next element from the same list into the heap, and continue until one list is exhausted.

mbpp_0531.reference_description: Write a function to find minimum number of coins that make a given value.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find minimum number of coins that make a given value.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Recursive Minimum Coin Change (no DP)
Main goal: Given coin denominations in coins[0..m-1], determine the minimum number of coins needed to make amount V using a naive recursive approach. It returns 0 when V is 0; otherwise it tries all coins ≤ V, recurses on V - coin, and tracks the smallest result plus one. If no combination works, it returns Integer.MAX_VALUE (no solution). No memoization or dynamic programming is used.

mbpp_0918.reference_description: Write a function to count coin change.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count coin change.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Coin Change - Count Ways to Make Change
Goal: Given coin denominations S (length m) and target n, this DP computes the number of distinct combinations to sum to n using unlimited coins from S (order-independent). It fills a 2D table where table[i][j] is the number of ways to make amount i with the first j+1 coin types, initializes table[0][*] = 1, and returns table[n][m-1].

mbpp_0702.reference_description: Write a function to find the minimum number of elements that should be removed such that amax-amin<=k.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the minimum number of elements that should be removed such that amax-amin<=k.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Minimum removals to keep a range of at most k
Main goal: Given an array, determine the smallest number of elements to remove so that the remaining elements have max - min <= k. The code sorts the array and, for each starting index i, finds the largest index j > i such that arr[j] - arr[i] <= k using a binary search (findInd). It then computes removals as n - (j - i + 1) and takes the minimum over all i. Note: there is a potential boundary issue in findInd that could prevent returning the true maximum j in some edge cases, possibly affecting the result.

mbpp_0819.reference_description: Write a function to count the frequency of consecutive duplicate elements in a given array of numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count the frequency of consecutive duplicate elements in a given array of numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Counts consecutive runs of equal integers in a list and returns a Result containing two parallel lists: elements (the distinct values encountered in order) and frequencies (the lengths of each run). The method assumes the input is sorted (or grouped) so duplicates are consecutive; it scans adjacent elements to build run-lengths. If the input is null or empty, it returns empty lists. The Result class exposes getters for both lists.

mbpp_0622.reference_description: Write a function to find the median of two sorted arrays of same size.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the median of two sorted arrays of same size.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Computes the median of two sorted arrays of equal length by merging them in order and tracking the two most recent values (m1, m2). It runs a merged traversal until it has processed n+1 elements, then returns the average of m1 and m2. The code uses indices i and j to walk through arr1 and arr2 and handles exhaustion of one array, but contains a bug: when one array is exhausted it incorrectly uses arr2[0] or arr1[0] instead of the current element, which can yield incorrect results.

mbpp_0448.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the sum of perrin numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate the sum of perrin numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Computes the sum of Perrin numbers P(0) through P(n) using an iterative recurrence P(k) = P(k-2) + P(k-3) with initial values P(0)=3, P(1)=0, P(2)=2; calSum(n) returns the running total of P(0)+...+P(n) and handles n = 0, 1, 2 as base cases.

mbpp_0141.reference_description: Write a function to sort array of elements using pancake sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort array of elements using pancake sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: Pancake Sort. Main goal: sort the input int[] in ascending order using the pancake sorting algorithm by repeatedly bringing the maximum of the unsorted prefix to the front, then to its final position with two flips; a helper flips a subarray in place.

mbpp_0714.reference_description: Write a java function to count the number of distinct power of prime factor of given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the number of distinct power of prime factor of given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Triangular-count from prime exponents

Main goal: Compute a value from the prime factorization of n: for each prime factor with exponent e, add the largest t with t(t+1)/2 ≤ e (i.e., the number of triangular numbers ≤ e); after removing all small factors, if a remaining prime factor exists, add 1. Return the total.

mbpp_0717.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the standard deviation.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate the standard deviation.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Compute mean and sample standard deviation
Main goal: Provide methods to compute the arithmetic mean of a double array and its sample standard deviation (unbiased, using n-1 in the denominator).
Functions:
- avgCalc: returns the mean of the array (special-cases length 1; note: empty arrays would cause an error).
- sdCalc: returns the sample standard deviation using the mean from avgCalc; returns 0 for arrays of length <= 1.

mbpp_0853.reference_description: Write a java function to find sum of odd factors of a number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find sum of odd factors of a number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Returns the sum of all odd divisors of the input n. It first removes all factors of 2, then factorizes the remaining odd part by trial division. For each odd prime factor p^a found, it multiplies the running result by (1 + p + p^2 + ... + p^a). If a remaining factor n > 1 exists, it multiplies by (1 + n). The final result is the sum of odd divisors of the original n.

mbpp_0131.reference_description: Write a java function to reverse only the vowels of a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to reverse only the vowels of a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Reverse Vowels in a String
Main goal: Return a new string with vowels reversed in place while consonants stay in their original positions; it collects vowels (both lower and upper case) and then fills them back in reverse order.

mbpp_0071.reference_description: Write a function to sort array of elements using comb sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort array of elements using comb sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Implements the comb sort algorithm to sort an int[] in ascending order in place. It starts with a gap equal to the array length and repeatedly reduces the gap by a shrink factor of 1.3, comparing elements gap positions apart and swapping if out of order. A swapped flag tracks whether any swaps occurred during a pass; the loop continues until the gap is 1 and no swaps occur, after which the sorted array is returned.

mbpp_0122.reference_description: Write a function to find n’th smart number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find n’th smart number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SmartNumberFinder - nth number with at least three distinct prime factors
Main goal: Return the nth smallest integer under MAX that has at least three distinct prime divisors, using a sieve-like method to count distinct prime factors and then selecting the nth such number after sorting.

mbpp_0374.reference_description: Write a function to print all permutations of a given string including duplicates.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to print all permutations of a given string including duplicates.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: String Permutations Generator
Main goal: Generate all unique permutations of the input string by recursively permuting the rest of the string and inserting the first character into every position of each permutation, collecting non-duplicate results in a list.

mbpp_0175.reference_description: Write a function to verify validity of a string of parentheses.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to verify validity of a string of parentheses.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Checks if the given string of parentheses/brackets is valid by using a stack to match opening symbols '(', '{', '[' with their corresponding closing symbols, returning true only if all are properly closed in correct order.

mbpp_0652.reference_description: Write a function to flatten the given tuple matrix into the tuple array with each tuple representing each column.

mbpp_0386.reference_description: Write a function to find out the minimum no of swaps required for bracket balancing in the given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find out the minimum no of swaps required for bracket balancing in the given string.

When encountering '[', if there is an imbalance, it adds that imbalance to the swap count and decreases imbalance; when encountering ']', it updates imbalance as countRight - countLeft. The returned value is the total swaps needed to balance the string.

mbpp_0846.reference_description: Write a function to find the minimum number of platforms required for a railway\/bus station.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the minimum number of platforms required for a railway\/bus station.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Computes the minimum number of platforms required at a station for given arrival and departure times. It sorts both arrays, then uses two pointers to simulate train arrivals and departures, increasing the platform count on an arrival before/dequeuing a departure, and decreasing it otherwise. The maximum simultaneous platforms needed is returned. Time complexity is O(n log n) due to sorting; space complexity is O(1) beyond input data.

mbpp_0395.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first non-repeated character in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first non-repeated character in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The goal is to find and return the first non-repeating character in a given string. It counts occurrences with a map while recording the order of first appearances in a list, then scans that list to return the first character with a count of 1 (or null if none).

mbpp_0001.reference_description: Write a function to find the minimum cost path to reach (m, n) from (0, 0) for the given cost matrix cost[][] and a position (m, n) in cost[][].

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the minimum cost path to reach (m, n) from (0, 0) for the given cost matrix cost[][] and a position (m, n) in cost[][].
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MinCostPath - Dynamic Programming for Minimum Cost Path

Main goal: Compute the minimum total cost to reach cell (m, n) from (0, 0) in the given cost matrix, allowing moves to the right, down, or diagonally down-right. It builds a DP table tc, initializes the first row and column with cumulative costs, and for each cell uses tc[i][j] = cost[i][j] + min(tc[i-1][j-1], tc[i-1][j], tc[i][j-1]); the result is tc[m][n].

mbpp_0829.reference_description: Write a function to find out the second most repeated (or frequent) string in the given sequence.

mbpp_0661.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum sum that can be formed which has no three consecutive elements present.

mbpp_0020.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given number is woodball or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given number is woodball or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:

Main goal: Determine whether a given odd integer x is a Woodall number (x = n*2^n - 1 for some n); return true if so, otherwise false.

mbpp_0070.reference_description: Write a function to find whether all the given tuples have equal length or not.

mbpp_0492.reference_description: Write a function to search an element in the given array by using binary search.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to search an element in the given array by using binary search.

mbpp_0506.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the permutation coefficient of given p(n, k).

mbpp_0721.reference_description: Write a function to find a path with the maximum average over all existing paths for the given square matrix of size n*n.

mbpp_0510.reference_description: Write a function to find the number of subsequences having product smaller than k for the given non negative array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the number of subsequences having product smaller than k for the given non negative array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Dynamic programming to count subsequences with product equal to k (with a noted bug)

Main goal: Compute the number of subsequences of the array arr whose product equals k, using a 2D DP where dp[i][j] is the count of subsequences from the first j elements with product i. The function noOfSubsequences(arr, k) returns dp[k][n].

How it works (brief): 
- dp is a (k+1) by (n+1) table initialized to zero. 
- For each target product i from 1 to k and for each prefix length j from 1 to n:
  - Start with dp[i][j] = dp[i][j-1] (skip arr[j-1]).
  - If arr[j-1] > 0 and arr[j-1] <= i, add dp[i / arr[j-1]][j-1] + 1 to dp[i][j], intended to account for including arr[j-1] (either extending a subsequence with product i/arr[j-1] or the single-element subsequence [arr[j-1]]).
- Returns dp[k][n].

Important note (buggy behavior): The code lacks a divisibility check (i % arr[j-1] == 0). Without it, including arr[j-1] can contribute to dp[i][j] even when i is not a multiple of arr[j-1], leading to incorrect counts. Also, the +1 term should only apply when i == arr[j-1] for single-element subsequences. Overall complexity is O(k*n) time and O(k*n) space.

Description: The check method iterates through consecutive elements, using a flag g to mark when a decrease has occurred. If a decrease has already occurred (g == 1) and a subsequent increase is found (arr[i] - arr[i - 1] > 0), it returns false. If a decrease is found (arr[i] - arr[i - 1] < 0), it sets g = 1. If no violation occurs, it returns true. Note: There is a bug—the code uses arr[i] - arr[i] < 0 in the second condition, which is always false; thus g never gets set and the function always returns true. It should be arr[i] - arr[i - 1] < 0.

mbpp_0672.reference_description: Write a function to find maximum of three numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find maximum of three numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxOfThree
Goal: Return the largest among three integers by comparing num1, num2, and num3 using conditional checks.

mbpp_0172.reference_description: Write a function to find the occurence of characters 'std' in the given string 1. array item 1. array item 1. array item 2. array item 2. array item 2. array item

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the occurence of characters 'std' in the given string 1. array item 1. array item 1. array item 2. array item 2. array item 2. array item
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Counts how many times the substring "std" appears in the input string by iterating over all consecutive 3-character windows and returns the total (0 if the string is shorter than 3).

mbpp_0227.reference_description: Write a function to find minimum of three numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find minimum of three numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MinOfThree - Return the minimum of three integers
Main goal: Implement a single utility method minOfThree(a, b, c) that returns the smallest of three int values using direct pairwise comparisons. It evaluates a first, then b, then c (a <= b && a <= c ? a : (b <= a && b <= c ? b : c)), providing O(1) time and deterministic behavior when values are equal.

mbpp_0438.reference_description: Write a function to count bidirectional tuple pairs.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count bidirectional tuple pairs.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Count bidirectional edge pairs in a list
Main goal: Given a list of directed edges represented as 2-element int arrays [u, v], count how many pairs of edges exist where one is the reverse of the other ([u, v] and [v, u]). The function checks all pairs with i < j, increments the count when the edges are reverses, and returns the final count as a string. Time complexity is O(n^2). Duplicate edges can produce multiple counts.

mbpp_0663.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest possible value of k such that k modulo x is y.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest possible value of k such that k modulo x is y.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Largest k in [0, n] with k mod x = y
Main goal: Brute-force search to find the maximum k ≤ n such that k % x == y; return -1 if none exists.
Notes: Since k % x ranges from 0 to x-1, y must be in [0, x-1]; otherwise the function returns -1. Time complexity is O(n).

mbpp_0876.reference_description: Write a java function to find lcm of two positive integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find lcm of two positive integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Brute-force Least Common Multiple calculator
Main goal: Compute the least common multiple (LCM) of two integers by starting from the larger of the two and incrementing until a number divisible by both x and y is found.

mbpp_0191.reference_description: Write a function to check whether the given month name contains 30 days or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether the given month name contains 30 days or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MonthUtils.checkMonthNumber
Main goal: Expose a utility method that returns true if the input month name is one of April, June, September, or November; otherwise false. Note: the method name is misleading (checks names, not numbers), it's case-sensitive, and can throw a NullPointerException if the input is null.

mbpp_0481.reference_description: Write a function to determine if there is a subset of the given set with sum equal to the given sum.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to determine if there is a subset of the given set with sum equal to the given sum.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Implements a classic recursive solution to the subset sum problem. Given an integer array and a target sum, isSubsetSum(set, n, sum) returns true if there exists a subset among the first n elements whose total equals sum. It uses base cases (sum == 0 -> true; n == 0 -> false) and recursively explores two possibilities for the last considered element: exclude it or include it (sum minus the element).

mbpp_0961.reference_description: Write a function to convert a roman numeral to an integer.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to convert a roman numeral to an integer.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Roman Numeral to Integer Converter
Main goal: Convert a Roman numeral string to its integer value by mapping characters to their values and applying the subtractive notation during a single left-to-right pass.

mbpp_0843.reference_description: Write a function to find the nth super ugly number from a given prime array of size k using heap queue algorithm.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the nth super ugly number from a given prime array of size k using heap queue algorithm.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Nth Super Ugly Number Generator using a Priority Queue
Main goal: Compute the nth super ugly number (numbers whose prime factors come only from the given primes) by using a min-heap of candidates. It keeps an array of generated ugly numbers starting with 1, repeatedly pops the smallest candidate, appends it if it's new, advances that candidate to the next multiple of its associated prime (prime * ugly[index+1]), and reinserts it into the heap. A Node stores (value, prime, index) to track each prime's current multiple.

mbpp_0520.reference_description: Write a function to find the lcm of the given array elements.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the lcm of the given array elements.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: LCMCalculator - computes the least common multiple
Main goal: Provide utilities to calculate the LCM of two integers and to compute the LCM of an array of integers by iteratively applying the two-number LCM.
Functions:
- findLcm(int num1, int num2): uses Euclidean algorithm to find gcd, then returns (num1 * num2) / gcd.
- getLcm(int[] l): computes the LCM of the array by repeatedly applying findLcm across elements.
Notes: Assumes positive inputs; may fail with zero or negative values and can overflow for large numbers.

mbpp_0018.reference_description: Write a function to remove characters from the first string which are present in the second string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to remove characters from the first string which are present in the second string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
StringUtil - Character-based string utilities
Main goal: Provide utilities to convert strings to/from character arrays, count character frequencies, and remove characters found in a given second string from a target string (i.e., filter out chars present in the second string).
